loginHelp: You will approve a short code in Beacon. No password is typed here.
deviceHelp: We opened {uri} in your browser. Check that it shows this code, then approve.
deviceScope: The server refused the requested permissions.
sessionExpired: Your session ended. Sign in again.
noTasks: No tasks yet. Tasks you can track time on appear here.
offline: Offline — {count} action(s) will be sent when the connection returns.
offlineStartNote: When the connection returns, the times are sent as they happened.
dropped: {count} offline action(s) could not be applied.
featureIdleText: Your server does not set this, so it is your choice (off by default). When on, the app reads only your computer's "time since last input" counter, on this device, while a timer runs, and asks you after the chosen minutes. Nothing about your activity is sent: only your answer.
featureNotificationsText: When on, the app may show a system notification (for example when you come back while a timer runs), never outside the working hours published by your organisation.
featureAutostart: Start TimeTrack when I sign in to my computer
featureAutostartText: Off by default. When on, the app starts hidden in the tray when you sign in to your computer. It does not start a timer.
privacyIntro: TimeTrack only records the time you choose to track.
privacyNever: Screenshots, keystrokes, the applications or windows you use, the pages you visit, your activity or idle state.
privacyRights: Your employer is responsible for the data on the server. You can see and export your entries in Beacon.
updateRequiredText: This version ({current}) is no longer supported by your server. Version {min} or later is required.
updateFailed: The automatic update failed: {message}. Download the new version from Beacon.
updateUnavailable: Your server asks for version {min} or later, but no compatible update is offered automatically. Download it from Beacon.
updateManual: Automatic updates are not available in this build. Download version {version} from Beacon.
deviceUntrusted: The server sent a sign-in address on another site, so it was not opened. Open it yourself only if you trust it:
serverHelp: The address you use to open Beacon in your browser.
whereText: Open Beacon in your browser and copy the address from the address bar (for example https://beacon.example.com). It is also on Beacon → Tasks → Time → Apps, next to the download of this app.
urlInvalid: That does not look like a web address. Example: beacon.example.com
urlCredentials: Remove the user name and password from the address.
urlInsecure: Beacon must use https://. Type the address with https://.
errGenericText: Try again. If it keeps happening, copy the details for support.
errUnreachableText: Check the address and your connection. If you use a VPN, connect it.
errNotBeaconText: TimeTrack was not found at {host}. Check that it is the same address you use in the browser.
errNoDeviceFlowTitle: This server doesn't support device sign-in yet
errNoDeviceFlowText: {host} answers, but it cannot connect devices with a code. Ask your administrator to update Beacon (TimeTrack 1.9 or later).
errRateLimitedText: Wait a moment and try again.
errTaskForbiddenText: You no longer have access to this task or its board.
errScopeText: Connect this computer again to grant them.
errTimerRunningText: It was started on another device. Retry to see it.
errServerText: It is not your fault. Try again in a moment.
codeExpiry: Time left to approve the code
deviceExpiredText: Get a new code and approve it in Beacon.
deviceDeniedTitle: The connection was declined in Beacon
deviceDeniedText: If that was a mistake, try again and approve the code.
searchHint: ↑ ↓ to choose, Enter to start, Esc to clear
noResults: No tasks match “{query}”. Only tasks you can track time on appear.
noRecent: Start a task and it will appear here. Pin the ones you use most.
shortcutHelp: Shows TimeTrack with the search open, from any app. Format: CommandOrControl+Alt+Shift+T.
shortcutFailed: Shortcut “{shortcut}” is in use or not valid — choose another.
aboutText: TimeTrack {version} for Beacon. Records only the time you choose to track.
stillThereTimeout: No rush. If there is no answer within {minutes} min, the timer pauses at your last activity and nothing is lost.
idleMeeting: I was in a meeting or call
idleKept: Got it, the time is kept.
idleDiscarded: Those minutes were left out. The timer keeps running.
idlePaused: Timer paused at your last activity.
idleNoteHelp: For example "Weekly sync". It is saved on this time entry.
awayText: It paused at {time}, your last activity on {task}. Welcome back whenever you are ready.
gapText: The timer paused at {from}, your last activity on {task}. You were away until {to} ({minutes} min). What should happen with that time?
gapKeep: It was work: add it to {task}
gapUnsupported: Your server cannot add past time from the app. You can add it in Beacon if you need to.
idleOrgOn: Turned on by your organisation. While a timer runs, after {minutes} minutes without keyboard or mouse input the app asks whether you are still there. You can make it wait longer.
idleLocalOnly: The input counter is read on this computer only and is never stored or sent. Only your answer reaches the server.
clamp_start_overlap: {task} started at {applied} instead of {requested}, when your previous entry ended.
clamp_start_max_backdate: {task} started at {applied} instead of {requested}: your organisation does not allow adding time further back.
clamp_start_future: {task} started at {applied}: the requested time ({requested}) was in the future. Check this computer's clock.
clamp_start_disabled: {task} started at {applied} instead of {requested}: your organisation does not allow adding past time.
clamp_start_not_supported: {task} was recorded from {applied}, when the connection returned. It started at {requested}, but your server cannot record earlier starts.
clamp_stop_before_start: The timer stopped at {applied}, when it started, instead of {requested}.
clamp_stop_future: The timer stopped at {applied}: the requested time ({requested}) was in the future. Check this computer's clock.
clamp_stop_disabled: The timer stopped at {applied} instead of {requested}: your organisation does not allow earlier stop times.
clamp_stop_none: The timer stopped at {applied} instead of {requested}.
localDataCleared: Local data cleared. TimeTrack keeps nothing on this computer now.
privacySentSignIn: The device name you approve in Beacon, when you sign in.
privacySentTimer: The task you start, stop or switch to, the time you did it (also for actions sent later, after being offline), an optional note and the source "desktop".
privacySentIdle: Your answer to "Still there?": keep, discard, pause or count on another task, with the start and end of that time. Never the input counter.
privacySentUpdates: The app version, platform and architecture when it checks for updates.
privacyLocalToken: The session token, in the system keychain.
privacyLocalState: The server address, your e-mail, the running timer, actions waiting to be sent, pinned tasks, the last task you tracked, an unsent meeting note, and your settings with the date of each consent.
privacyLocalIdle: The "time since last input" counter: read from the system every 30 seconds while a timer runs, used only to decide when to ask, never stored, logged or sent.
privacyLocalTotals: The Today and This week totals, computed here from your own entries.
clearLocalText: Signs you out and deletes everything TimeTrack keeps on this computer: the token, settings, consents, pinned tasks, actions waiting to be sent and the "Still there?" state. Your entries on the server are not touched.
clearLocalSure: Delete all TimeTrack data on this computer?
clearLocalPending: {count} action(s) have not reached the server yet and will be lost. Delete all TimeTrack data on this computer?
